dek: New tools expose hidden model knowledge, quantify the enterprise deployment gap, and open up full-duplex voice agents—while efficiency gains keep compounding.
brief: Honest measurement is today’s theme. A forensic interrogation method can now distinguish model sandbagging from genuine ignorance, while EnterpriseVal quantifies the gap between frontier capability and measurable business value. NVIDIA’s NemotronLabs opens full-duplex speech-to-speech with native tool calling, and new releases push block pruning and tokenization efficiency sharply forward.

top_stories.title: A lie detector test for language models
top_stories.summary: A new paper adapts the Concealed Information Test from forensic psychology to detect whether a language model is hiding knowledge it holds or simply does not have it.
top_stories.why: sandbagging on capability evaluations has been a suspicion without a measurement. This gives evaluators a test for the gap between reported and actual capability—the credibility problem at the heart of every safety evaluation.

top_stories.title: EnterpriseVal quantifies the capability–value gap
top_stories.summary: Frontier models can produce professional deliverables that expert graders judge comparable to human work on a substantial share of economically valuable tasks, yet most enterprise GenAI initiatives still show no measurable business effect.
top_stories.why: the bottleneck is no longer model capability. It is deployment, reliability, and value capture: agents that can do the work still cannot prove the return.

top_stories.title: NemotronLabs opens full-duplex voice with tool calling
top_stories.summary: NVIDIA’s open VoiceChat model combines a streaming speech encoder with a decoder-only language model, using parallel output streams for agent text and structured function calls.
top_stories.why: full-duplex voice agents with native tool use have been a closed-model story. An open release with function calling puts that stack in everyone’s hands.

top_stories.title: Pruning LLMs like a physicist
top_stories.summary: Multiverse Computing reframes transformer-block removal as a constrained binary optimization mapped onto an Ising spin glass. At 50% compression of Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, the method beats the strongest competing block-removal approach by about 23 MMLU points.
top_stories.why: depth pruning is becoming a principled search problem rather than a heuristic hack, and the method generalizes to hybrid attention architectures.

blogs.body: Hugging Face (Sep 21) — Pruning LLMs Like a Physicist: Block Removal as an Ising Optimization Problem: minimizing the spin system’s energy becomes a cheap proxy for downstream benchmark quality, allowing billions of block-removal configurations to be searched without benchmarking each one. Code is open-sourced.

Hugging Face (Sep 21) — tokenizers v1: encode, decode and scaling, measured: the release candidate produces identical token IDs as v0.23 while encoding 3–30× faster on an Apple M4 Max and scaling at 76% of linear across eight workers. A SIMD splitter, thread-local cache, allocation-free merge loop, native parallelism, and the tokbench harness drive the gains.

papers.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won’t Reveal
papers.body: Hiskias Dingeto — models can hold knowledge they do not report; the forensic Concealed Information Test is adapted to detect whether a model is hiding an answer or simply does not have one.

papers.title: EnterpriseVal: Quantifying the Efficacy, Reliability and Value of Generative AI in the Enterprise
papers.body: Abbas Raza Ali, Muhammad Ajmal Siddiqui, Moona Zahid — frontier models match human professional work on a substantial share of economically valuable tasks, yet most enterprise GenAI initiatives fail to show measurable business effect.

papers.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
papers.body: Jagadeesh Balam et al. — an open streaming speech encoder plus decoder-only language model uses parallel output streams for agent text and structured function calls, with an auxiliary RNN-T branch.

papers.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself
papers.body: Bowen Ye et al. — mines diverse reinforcement-learning tasks with reliable verifiers directly from open-source codebases instead of relying on issues and commits.

papers.title: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments
papers.body: Mingfei Gao et al. — a family of vision-language models at 2B, 4B, and 8B parameters unifies UI grounding, multi-step navigation across mobile, desktop, and web, and visual tool use.

papers.title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw
papers.body: Renkai Ma et al. — analysis of 73,093 first-person Reddit posts about OpenClaw use finds the human values people prioritize when delegating; evaluations should measure values, not only task completion.

papers.title: SpecQuant: Speculative Decoding with Multi-Parent Quantization for Adaptive LLM Inference
papers.body: Harish KB et al. — combines quantization, speculative decoding, and adaptive inference to run language models on consumer hardware without per-architecture retraining.

papers.title: Abstention and Noise Filtering: Two Missing Primitives of Softmax Attention
papers.body: Richard Zhe Wang — gating the value pathway gives softmax attention two missing primitives, abstention and noise filtering; experiments disentangle which effect explains the pretraining gains.

threads.name: Agentic reliability
threads.update: The stack keeps thickening: the Lie-Detector Test adds a measurement primitive for hidden knowledge, CodeMidas adds training infrastructure, MintAct adds a unified visual-agent family, and the OpenClaw values study reframes delegation around human values rather than task completion. Measurement → detection → design → training → values, all in one day.

threads.name: Agent misalignment goes public
threads.update: The Lie-Detector Test is the natural measurement tool for this thread: sandbagging in capability evaluations was previously a suspicion without a test. OpenAI’s six misalignment reports raised the credibility question; now there is a forensic method aimed at it.

threads.name: Efficiency race
threads.update: Three wins in one day: Ising-optimization block pruning adds 23 MMLU points at 50% compression, tokenizers v1 encodes up to 30× faster with 76% linear scaling, and SpecQuant combines quantization with speculative decoding for consumer hardware. Cheaper to train, cheaper to serve.

threads.name: Lab supremacy race
threads.update: Open-model flank activity: NVIDIA’s NemotronLabs released an open full-duplex voice model with native tool calling, competing directly with closed voice-agent stacks.

threads.name: OpenAI monetization
threads.update: Quiet today; the Sep 23 Shopify app launch is the next milestone.
